How much does it cost to run an oil-filled radiator?

Oil-filled radiators hold heat well, but every kWh of heat costs a kWh of electricity. That makes them expensive compared with gas central heating or a heat pump.

Cost per day
£1.26
About £230 a year at 4 hours per day, 7 days a week, 6 months a year.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

A typical oil-filled radiator uses about 2,000 watts (500–2,500W depending on the model). Used for 4 hours per day, 7 days a week, for 6 months of the year, it costs about £1.26 per day and £230 a year at the current price cap rate.

Source for the typical figure: CSE 'What uses watt?' table. See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Use the thermostat rather than the highest setting.
  • Heat one room with the door closed.
  • For long-term heating, compare against a heat pump, which gives around three times more heat per kWh.

Questions

How much does it cost to run an oil-filled radiator per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 2000W model costs about 32p an hour, allowing for it running at full power about 60% of the time.

How much does it cost to run an oil-filled radiator per year?

About £230 a year, based on 4 hours per day, 7 days a week, 6 months a year. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my oil-filled radiator's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
